sources.entry: Cocoa-Way - Wayland compositor for running Linux GUI apps without a virtual machine. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/J-x-Z/cocoa-way) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A native macOS Wayland compositor that presents Linux GUI applications through a Metal renderer, without running a full virtual machine desktop.
summary.what_it_does: Cocoa-Way receives the Wayland protocol on macOS and shows Linux applications via a Metal renderer. It can connect to an existing Linux machine over SSH with Waypipe, or manage local GUI applications through Apple Container, Docker-compatible engines, and OrbStack. Applications are organized as saved profiles, running instances, and displays, with Desktop mode (one compositor window) and Rootless mode (each xdg-toplevel becomes its own macOS window). It forwards clipboard (text and PNG), CoreAudio audio, keyboard, pointer and gestures. A local control API is provided through the cocoa-wayctl CLI (with JSON output) and an optional MCP stdio adapter that is read-only by default. Version 2.1 adds an opt-in desktop background behind macOS app windows.
use_cases: Run Linux GUI apps on a Mac without a virtual machine
Connect to a remote Linux host and show its apps over SSH
Launch GUI containers from Apple Container, Docker, or OrbStack on macOS
Use a nested Linux compositor such as niri or Hyprland on a Mac
Diagnose and script Linux app containers from the command line or an AI agent
how_to_run: cargo build --release (after brew install libxkbcommon pkg-config and cloning the repo)
notable: Apple Container Transport V2 multiplexes Waypipe streams over a published Unix socket, with a stdio relay fallback
Opt-in Desktop Background places a Linux desktop behind ordinary macOS app windows (experimental)
cocoa-wayctl --json gives scriptable status, diagnostics, logs and performance data over a local control socket
MCP adapter is read-only by default; --allow-control enables only app launch/stop and display create/close, never deletion or arbitrary commands
Bidirectional clipboard including PNG images up to 64 MiB
caveats: Requires macOS 26 on Apple silicon for the Apple Container runtime; Waypipe must be installed on both the Mac and the Linux side
No guest GPU passthrough under Apple Container, so Linux apps render with Mesa/CPU before upload to Metal; Vulkan is not in this release
Release apps are ad-hoc signed, not Apple-notarized; end-to-end input and display latency is still under investigation
keywords: run linux gui apps on mac
run firefox on mac from linux
